answer: Latency escrow scoring ties each identity to a slowly accrued reputation balance that only pays out after sustained low-dispute activity. A pearl of verified history takes months of consistent behavior to form, and any fork must rebuild it independently before earning throughput rights. Every clone therefore pays the full time-and-work cost of reaccrual while the original keeps its violet score intact. An attacker cloning ten thousand identities pays ten thousand parallel accrual periods plus lost escrow on any flagged pair, a walnut of overhead that dwarfs honest participation.
